name: Tropic Trooper
affiliation_detail:
Tropic Trooper is assessed as a Chinese state-sponsored group based on its sustained targeting of Taiwan, the Philippines, and Hong Kong — regions of direct strategic interest to the PRC — as well as its use of tools and TTPs common to the Chinese APT ecosystem (China Chopper, Poison Ivy, TClient). (Trend Micro, 2015; Kaspersky, 2024) No specific MSS bureau, PLA unit, or contractor has been publicly identified.
Kaspersky noted potential connections between Tropic Trooper and the FamousSparrow threat group. (Kaspersky, 2024)
description:
Tropic Trooper is a suspected Chinese state-sponsored cyber espionage group active since at least 2011, targeting primarily government, military, healthcare, transportation, and technology organizations in Taiwan, the Philippines, and Hong Kong. (Trend Micro, 2015; MITRE, n.d.)
The group first gained public attention through Trend Micro's 2015 "Operation Tropic Trooper" report, which documented campaigns against Taiwanese government institutions and Philippine military targets using weaponized document exploits. The "KeyBoy" alias derives from early malware samples used to target the Tibetan community and parliamentary staff. (Citizen Lab, 2016)
Tropic Trooper is notable for its capability to penetrate air-gapped military networks. In 2020, Trend Micro documented USBferry, a USB malware active since at least December 2014 that targets physically isolated environments in the Taiwanese and Philippine military. The group was observed pivoting from a military hospital into air-gapped networks to exfiltrate defense-, ocean-, and ship-related documents. (Trend Micro, 2020) In 2021, Trend Micro identified the group expanding into the transportation sector, accessing flight schedules and financial data from compromised hosts. (Trend Micro, 2021)
In 2024, Kaspersky documented the group targeting a Middle Eastern government entity involved in human rights studies — "particularly those related to the Israel-Hamas war" — since at least June 2023. (Kaspersky, 2024) 
In April 2026, Zscaler ThreatLabz and Itochu researchers identified campaigns using trojanized SumatraPDF with military-themed lures and AdaptixC2 beacons leveraging GitHub for C2, targeting individuals in Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea. (Zscaler, 2026; Dark Reading, 2026)

campaigns.name: Operation Tropic Trooper
campaigns.description: Trend Micro documented the group's initial campaigns targeting Taiwanese government institutions and Philippine military entities using spear-phishing with weaponized document exploits. The campaign name became the group's primary designation. (Trend Micro, 2015)

campaigns.name: USBferry Air-Gapped Network Targeting
campaigns.description: Trend Micro documented USBferry, a USB malware active since December 2014, targeting physically isolated military networks in Taiwan and the Philippines. The group pivoted from military hospitals into air-gapped environments and exfiltrated defense, naval, and shipping documents. Three USBferry versions were identified, with the latest residing entirely in memory. Targets included military/navy agencies, government institutions, and a national bank. (Trend Micro, 2020)

sources.title: Tropic Trooper's Back: USBferry Attack Targets Air-gapped Environments

campaigns.name: Earth Centaur Transportation Sector Campaign
campaigns.description: Trend Micro documented Tropic Trooper expanding to target the transportation sector in Taiwan, the Philippines, and Hong Kong. The group accessed flight schedules, financial plans, and personal information from compromised hosts. Backdoors used reverse proxy protocols to bypass network security monitoring. (Trend Micro, 2021)

campaigns.name: Middle East Government Targeting (Human Rights)
campaigns.description: Kaspersky documented a year-long campaign (June 2023–2024) targeting a Middle Eastern government entity involved in human rights studies, "particularly those related to the Israel-Hamas war." The group deployed a China Chopper web shell variant embedded in Umbraco CMS, the Crowdoor loader (related to SparrowDoor), and DLL side-loading implants. A Malaysian government entity was simultaneously targeted. Kaspersky attributed with high confidence and noted this represented "a new strategic move" for the group. (Kaspersky, 2024)

sources.title: New Malicious Web Shell from the Tropic Trooper Group

campaigns.name: Trojanized SumatraPDF / AdaptixC2 Campaign
campaigns.description: Zscaler ThreatLabz identified Tropic Trooper distributing trojanized SumatraPDF installers bundled with military-themed decoy documents to target Chinese-speaking individuals in Taiwan and individuals in South Korea and Japan. The group used GitHub as a C2 platform for custom AdaptixC2 Beacons. Itochu researchers additionally discovered an exposed S3 bucket containing 48 files with new malware and phishing pages mimicking Signal authentication. (Zscaler, 2026; Itochu via Dark Reading, 2026)
